designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Smart inversion: the stamp leans about 4 degrees while the tower stands plumb, and the 3.97° denomination is a quiet in-joke. That lifts it above a souvenir-shop stamp. The tower linework is clean and confident in one ink, and it holds up well inverted on the black tee. Execution lets the gag down, though. The plumb tower base sits on the tilted ground line, so it reads as a drafting error rather than a deliberate move. The dashed road line and clip-art grass tufts look generic next to the careful architecture. The top-left perforation corner has a lumpy notch where the scallops don't resolve. Also, both mockups show an unrotated stamp, so the concept isn't what's being shown on the tee.
designs.fix: Make the joke unmistakable and clean. Give the tower its own level plinth, or a short plumb-line or spirit-level tick, so the frame clearly tilts around a straight tower. Replace the road dashes and tufts with a simple paved piazza band. Redraw the perforation corners symmetrically, then regenerate the mockups from the rotated art.
